note: Content digests of everything that decides whether the test suite runs, and of the suites themselves. A TRIPWIRE WITH NO SELF-ANCHOR on two distinct axes, both confirmed by independent runs. (1) A commit editing a file and its digest together passes; independent review proved this is a fixed-point property of a repository where one commit can change every file. (2) A guard invoked by `npm run check` cannot constrain a `check` that never invokes it. A trailing `&` backgrounds the chain so the shell returns 0 before any exit code matters, and replacing every `&&` with `||` short-circuits at step 1 so nothing after it runs at all -- including this guard. Requiring the guard to be the FIRST step (exit 81) catches demotion but not non-invocation. The remedy for (2) belongs to the CALLER: .github/workflows/ci.yml must run `node scripts/verify-test-coverage-floor.mjs` as its own workflow step rather than relying on a single `npm run check`. That file is owned by WP-0A-A0-001 and is read-only to the packages that found this, so it is referred to the Integration Owner under the RFC path. Both anchors are outside the repository: human review of the diff (RFC-2026-002) and protected CI, an open Gate G0 requirement.
cross_package_note: Any package that adds a test file must add it here, because the guard requires every discovered test file to be digested. This is a deliberate coupling: an unprotected suite can be gutted with the manifest byte-identical. It surfaced when WP-0A-CON-002 added three contract suites and CI failed at exit 87 while a local run on the unrebased branch passed - GitHub tests the MERGE of head into base, so a stacked branch that has not been rebased does not see its own integration.
